note.explanation: A catalyst makes a reaction faster by providing a different reaction path with a lower activation energy. More reactant molecules can then form products.
examples: Nickel acts as a catalyst in the hydrogenation of oil to give banaspati ghee.
Platinum acts as a catalyst in the production of H₂SO₄.
note.checkAnswer: It lowers the activation energy, so the reaction rate increases.
note.simple: A catalyst gives reacting molecules an easier path to products, so the reaction happens faster.
note.checkQuestion: How does a catalyst increase the rate of a reaction?
note.title: How reactions take place
steps: Reactant molecules move randomly and collide.
Only collisions involving molecules with enough energy can form the transition state.
The transition state can change into products or return to reactants.
A catalyst lowers the activation energy by changing the reaction path.
note.answer: Reactant molecules collide. If they have enough energy, they can form a transition state, which may then form products.

options: The energy needed for reactant molecules to form a transition state
The energy released when products form
The energy possessed by every reactant molecule
The energy difference between the reactants and the container walls
mcqs.stem: What is the activation energy of a reaction?
rationales: Correct: activation energy is absorbed by reactant molecules to be converted into the transition state.
Incorrect: this describes energy release, not the activation energy.
Incorrect: molecules have different kinetic energies, and activation energy is not the energy of every molecule.
Incorrect: the container walls are not part of the definition of activation energy.

options: It changes the reaction path and substantially decreases activation energy.
It increases the energy of the products.
It is permanently used up during the reaction.
It prevents reactant molecules from colliding.
mcqs.stem: How does a catalyst increase the rate of a reaction, according to this section?
rationales: Correct: the changed path has lower activation energy, allowing more reactants to form products.
Incorrect: the section explains a change in activation energy, not an increase in product energy.
Incorrect: a catalyst increases reaction rate without undergoing permanent chemical change.
Incorrect: a catalyst does not stop collisions; it makes more collisions effective.

options: At the peak of the energy profile
At the reactant energy level
At the product energy level in every reaction
Below the reactant energy level
mcqs.stem: Where is the transition state shown on an energy profile diagram?
rationales: Correct: the transition state is shown at the peak of the curve.
Incorrect: this is the starting energy level of the reactants.
Incorrect: the product level is at the end of the curve and is not always the transition state.
Incorrect: the transition state is at the peak, not below the reactants.

options: Most reactant molecules have enough energy to overcome the activation energy.
The catalyst makes the reactants stop moving.
The products have no energy.
The transition state becomes impossible to form.
mcqs.stem: Why can lowering activation energy increase the rate of a reaction?
rationales: Correct: more reactant molecules can then reach the transition state and form products.
Incorrect: a catalyst does not stop molecular motion.
Incorrect: the products do not have zero energy as a result of catalysis.
Incorrect: a catalyst provides a path to the transition state rather than preventing it.

options: A₂ + B₂ → transition state → 2AB
A₂ + B₂ → 2AB without any collisions
2AB → A₂ + B₂ only
A₂ → B₂ → AB
mcqs.stem: Which sequence best represents the reaction process described for A₂ + B₂ → 2AB?
rationales: Correct: reactant molecules collide to form a transition state, which may lead to products.
Incorrect: the section says reactant molecules collide to produce the transition state.
Incorrect: this gives only a possible reverse direction and leaves out the stated forward process.
Incorrect: this sequence does not represent the stated reactants or transition state correctly.

options: It can either return to reactants or change into products.
It must always form products.
It must always return to reactants.
It remains unchanged permanently.
mcqs.stem: What can happen to the transition state after a very short time?
rationales: Correct: the section says it either returns to reactants or changes into products.
Incorrect: the transition state does not always proceed to products.
Incorrect: the transition state does not always return to reactants.
Incorrect: it exists for a very short period and does not remain unchanged permanently.

options: A substance that increases reaction rate without itself undergoing permanent chemical change
A substance that is permanently consumed to form products
A substance that always increases the enthalpy change
A substance that prevents the transition state from forming
mcqs.stem: Which statement correctly describes a catalyst?
rationales: Correct: this is the definition of a catalyst given in the section.
Incorrect: a catalyst does not undergo permanent chemical change.
Incorrect: the section links catalysts to activation energy and rate, not to increasing enthalpy change.
Incorrect: a catalyst lowers the activation energy for a reaction path that reaches the transition state.

options: The activation energy is substantially decreased.
The reactant and product energy levels become equal.
The transition state is removed from the reaction path.
The catalyst converts all reactant molecules into products at once.
mcqs.stem: What change does a catalyst make to the energy profile described in this section?
rationales: Correct: the catalysed path has a lower activation energy.
Incorrect: the catalyst does not necessarily make the energy levels of reactants and products equal.
Incorrect: the transition state remains part of the reaction path.
Incorrect: a catalyst increases the rate but does not convert all reactants at once.

written.text: Why is breaking of a bond an endothermic process?
written.finalAnswer: Energy must be absorbed to overcome the attraction between the bonded atoms and break the bond.

written.text: Explain why the reaction between atmospheric gases oxygen and nitrogen does not take place under normal conditions? But in the presence of lightning these gases react to give NO. The reaction stops as soon as the lightning stops.
written.finalAnswer: Under normal conditions, oxygen and nitrogen molecules do not have enough energy to overcome the activation energy. Lightning supplies energy so the molecules can form the transition state and react to give NO. When the lightning stops, the energy supply stops, so the reaction stops.

written.text: A reaction between natural gas (CH₄) and atmospheric oxygen does not take place when you mix them. As soon as you show a burning match stick, the reaction starts immediately and then it continues until one or both of the reactants is/are used up. Explain.
written.finalAnswer: Mixing CH₄ and oxygen at normal conditions does not give the molecules enough energy to overcome activation energy. The burning match supplies the needed energy to start the reaction. Once started, the exothermic reaction releases heat, which provides energy for further reaction, so it continues until one or both reactants are used up.

written.text: Explain the following terms. Activation energy, Transition state, Aerobic respiration
written.finalAnswer: Activation energy is the energy absorbed by reactant or product molecules to be converted into the transition state. The transition state is a short-lived state at the peak of the energy profile, which can return to reactants or proceed to products. Aerobic respiration is respiration that uses oxygen to release energy from food.

written.text: Why is it essential to cook some of the food items while others we can eat without cooking?
written.finalAnswer: Cooking supplies heat energy that can help overcome activation energy and bring about changes in food, including making some foods safe or easier to digest. Some foods can be eaten without cooking because they are already suitable to eat in their uncooked state.

examTips: A short-answer question may ask for the definitions of activation energy or a catalyst; use the textbook wording accurately.

For an energy-profile question, marks are commonly earned by correctly showing reactant and product energy levels, the transition-state peak, and the activation-energy label.
When asked how a catalyst speeds a reaction, state both that it changes the path and that it decreases activation energy.

example.question: For the hypothetical reaction A₂ + B₂ → 2AB, describe how the reaction takes place.
example.answer: The reactant molecules collide. A collision with enough energy may produce the transition state, which may then return to reactants or form products.

explain.title: Molecules move and collide
explain.body: Reactant molecules are in random motion and have different kinetic energies. They collide with one another, but collisions involving molecules with average or less than average kinetic energy may not produce a reaction.

explain.title: The transition state
explain.body: The textbook says: “The transition state is shown at the peak of curve in Fig (5.4).” A transition state exists for a very short time and may return to reactants or proceed to products.

explain.title: Activation energy
explain.body: The textbook defines it this way: “The energy absorbed by the reactant or product molecules in order to be converted into the transition state is called the activation energy (Eₐ) of the reaction.”

explain.title: Catalysts speed up reactions
explain.body: The textbook defines a catalyst as: “a substance that increases the rate of a chemical reaction without itself undergoing any permanent chemical change.” A catalyst changes the path of the reaction and substantially decreases activation energy, so more reactants can form products.

mistakes: Do not say that every collision causes a reaction; many collisions do not have enough energy.
Do not confuse activation energy with the difference in energy between reactants and products.
Do not say a catalyst is permanently used up; it does not undergo permanent chemical change.
Do not say a catalyst speeds a reaction by increasing activation energy. It decreases activation energy.
On an energy profile, do not label the product level as the transition state; the transition state is at the peak.
